name: Sun
shortDescription: Our home star, the source of nearly all energy that sustains life on Earth.

facts.distance: About 149.6 million km from Earth · 8 light-minutes 20 seconds
facts.color: White from space; often appears yellow from Earth
facts.stage: Main sequence · fusing hydrogen into helium
facts.composition: A sphere of plasma made mostly of hydrogen and helium, with smaller amounts of heavier elements.
features: Its gravity holds the Solar System together.
Magnetic activity produces sunspots, flares, and coronal mass ejections.
The visible photosphere lies below the chromosphere and extremely hot corona.
curiosities: The Sun contains more than 99.8% of the Solar System's mass.
Its core reaches roughly 15 million °C.
It is about halfway through its main-sequence lifetime.
facts.sunComparison: This is the reference star: stellar masses, radii, and luminosities are often measured in units of the Sun.
facts.systemNote: Eight planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, comets, and other objects orbit the Sun.

name: Sirius
shortDescription: The brightest star in Earth's night sky and the brilliant primary of a binary system.

facts.composition: Hot hydrogen-rich plasma, with energy produced through core hydrogen fusion.
features: It is the brightest star visible in Earth's night sky.
Sirius A is orbited by Sirius B, a compact white dwarf.
The pair completes an orbit in roughly half a century.
curiosities: Sirius is often called the Dog Star.
Its brightness comes from both its intrinsic power and its closeness to Earth.
Sirius B has almost the Sun's mass packed into an Earth-sized body.
facts.sunComparison: Sirius A is about twice as massive, almost twice as wide, and around 25 times as luminous as the Sun.
facts.systemNote: Sirius is a binary system composed of Sirius A and the white dwarf Sirius B.

source.label: NASA Science — Astronomers Weigh the Dog Star's Companion

name: Vega
shortDescription: A nearby, rapidly rotating star and one corner of the Summer Triangle.

facts.radius: About 2.4 times the Sun on average
facts.composition: Hydrogen-rich plasma undergoing core fusion, surrounded by a broad debris disk.
features: Vega rotates so rapidly that it is wider at the equator than at the poles.
Its poles are hotter and brighter than its equatorial region.
Infrared observations reveal a large disk of dust around it.
curiosities: Vega was once Earth's northern pole star and will be again because Earth's axis slowly precesses.
It helped define historical astronomical brightness scales.
It forms the Summer Triangle with Altair and Deneb.
facts.sunComparison: Vega is roughly twice the Sun's mass, more than twice its radius, and about 40 times as luminous.
facts.systemNote: No confirmed planets are known, but its debris disk is an important laboratory for planetary-system studies.

source.label: NASA Science — Tiny Particles, So Far Away

name: Betelgeuse
shortDescription: A vast, variable red supergiant marking Orion's shoulder.

facts.radius: Hundreds of times the Sun; commonly estimated near 700 solar radii
facts.luminosity: Roughly 100,000 times the Sun, varying over time
facts.composition: A massive evolved star with a hot core and enormous, cool, unstable outer layers that lose gas and dust.
features: It is one of the few stars whose surface and extended atmosphere can be directly studied.
Its brightness changes as the star pulsates and its surface evolves.
A major surface mass ejection contributed to its dramatic 2019–2020 dimming.
curiosities: Placed at the center of our Solar System, it would extend beyond the orbit of Mars in many estimates.
Its future supernova would be spectacular but is not expected to threaten Earth.
Despite its size, its surface is cooler than the Sun's.
facts.sunComparison: Betelgeuse is far younger than the Sun but vastly larger and more luminous because it began life with much more mass.
facts.systemNote: Recent observations indicate that Betelgeuse may have a close stellar companion, while its vast atmosphere continuously sheds material.

name: Rigel
shortDescription: A brilliant blue supergiant shining from Orion's foot.

facts.composition: A massive, very hot evolved star dominated by hydrogen and helium plasma.
features: Rigel is usually the brightest star in Orion.
It radiates much of its energy in ultraviolet wavelengths.
Its apparent single point of light belongs to a multiple-star system.
curiosities: Its light reaching Earth today began its journey centuries ago.
Rigel's short life is a consequence of consuming nuclear fuel extremely quickly.
It will eventually end as a core-collapse supernova.
facts.sunComparison: Rigel is around 20 times as massive, at least 70 times as wide, and about 120,000 times as luminous as the Sun.
facts.systemNote: Rigel is the dominant member of a multiple-star system with much fainter companions.

source.label: NASA Science — Universe Glossary: Blue Supergiants

name: Polaris
shortDescription: The current North Star and a pulsating beacon in a triple-star system.

facts.composition: An evolved hydrogen-and-helium star whose outer layers rhythmically expand and contract.
features: It lies close to the direction of Earth's north rotational axis.
Its pulsations cause predictable brightness changes.
The Polaris system contains at least three stars.
curiosities: Polaris is useful for navigation because it appears nearly fixed while the northern sky rotates around it.
It has not always been—and will not always be—the North Star.
Cepheid stars help astronomers measure cosmic distances.
facts.sunComparison: Polaris A is several times more massive, dozens of times larger, and thousands of times more luminous than the Sun.
facts.systemNote: Polaris A is accompanied by a close star, Polaris Ab, and a more distant companion, Polaris B.

source.label: NASA Science — There's More to the North Star Than Meets the Eye

name: Proxima Centauri
shortDescription: The nearest known star to the Sun: a small, faint, active red dwarf.

facts.composition: A cool, fully convective hydrogen-rich star with strong magnetic activity.
features: It is the closest known star beyond the Sun.
Powerful flares can make it brighten dramatically.
It belongs gravitationally to the Alpha Centauri stellar system.
curiosities: It is too faint to see with the unaided eye.
At least two confirmed planets orbit it, including Proxima Centauri b.
Red dwarfs can remain on the main sequence far longer than Sun-like stars.
facts.sunComparison: Proxima has only about one-eighth of the Sun's mass and emits roughly one-thousandth as much light.
facts.systemNote: Proxima is the distant third member of the Alpha Centauri system and hosts a compact planetary system.

name: Antares
shortDescription: The reddish heart of Scorpius and one of the sky's most recognizable supergiants.

facts.luminosity: Tens of thousands of times the Sun
facts.composition: A massive evolved star with an extended cool atmosphere, strong stellar winds, and a hot fusion-driven interior.
features: Its reddish color inspired a name meaning rival of Mars.
It marks the heart of the constellation Scorpius.
Antares has a much hotter, blue-white companion star.
curiosities: Its diameter would extend beyond Mars's orbit in many scale comparisons.
NASA's Cassini spacecraft used Antares during stellar occultation studies of Saturn's rings.
Like Betelgeuse, Antares is expected to end its life as a supernova.
facts.sunComparison: Antares is only several times more massive than the Sun but hundreds of times wider and tens of thousands of times more luminous.
facts.systemNote: Antares A and its smaller hot companion Antares B form a binary system.

source.label: NASA Science — July Night Sky Notes: Spy the Scorpion
